result.scientific_strategy:
## abd93958-a0b2-4d26-b212-96ebeb401d22 / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The campaign objective is at least 98% success, or 196 of 200 episodes, on the unchanged official two-joint-arm reach-and-hold task. Experiment 1's fresh PPO baseline reached 97.0% on the researcher panel and 98.0% on the protected task-reference panel at checkpoint-100352, with endpoint regression on both panels. Experiment 2 transferred that policy while expanding training to the official 6-20 cm radius range; its checkpoint-100352 reached 97.0% and 98.5% on the two development panels and remains the strongest measured artifact. Experiments 3, 4, 7, and 8 did not improve it: joint shaping, focused sampling, unchanged continuation, and full hold-credit forfeiture all produced candidates below the working policy on at least one panel, and experiment 8 was below it on both panels at every measured checkpoint. Experiments 5 and 6 repeated the unchanged full-radius recipe from fresh seeds and reached only 63.5-67.5% and 62.5-67.0% on the researcher panel, with task-reference ranges of 64.5-66.5% and 63.5-66.5%. The campaign therefore contains one useful transferred trajectory, two poor fresh trajectories, no robust cross-panel attainment, and no causal separation of transfer history from seed-dependent optimization. The hold-credit explanation was tested with complete interruption forfeiture and produced no measured progress under the transferred recipe. This remains provisional memory for reassessment and prescribes no next action.

**Lessons and limits:** Measured task success, rather than logged reward or training success, is the policy-progress signal. Checkpoint choice and training trajectory matter: experiments 1-3 selected earlier or intermediate candidates over endpoints, and experiments 4, 6, 7, and 8 showed proxy or late-training signals without task improvement. Experiment 2's full-radius transfer recovered two of experiment 1's four short-radius negative-angle failures, but left failures at 9.4-9.9 cm near -123 to -128 degrees and at 18.2 cm/-154.8 degrees. Later shaping, focused sampling, unchanged continuation, and hold-credit forfeiture did not robustly remove that residual region. Experiment 8 scored 96.0%, 95.0%, and 96.0% on the researcher panel and 97.0%, 96.5%, and 96.0% on task-reference at its measured checkpoints, versus the working policy's 97.0% and 98.5%; paired comparisons had no researcher-panel wins and protected-panel losses exceeded wins at every checkpoint. The fresh runs had broad target-geometry failures, unlike the retained policy's narrow residual pattern. The retained artifact and current method use the same 11-value observation containing joint state, Cartesian target error, both inverse-kinematics branch errors, direct two-joint actions, and saved observation normalization, so transfer is semantically compatible rather than merely dimension-compatible. Late-log evidence also shows materially different entropy and learning trajectories across the successful transferred run and poor fresh runs, but these are correlational. These observations reinforce the proxy/task mismatch and leave seed variance, transfer history, PPO optimization, and policy limitation confounded. The fixed 200-episode panels are development evidence, not the official final assessment.

**Open questions:** It remains unresolved whether the selected policy's residual failures reflect PPO update dynamics, target coverage, or a policy limitation; the tested sampling, shaping, continuation, and forfeiture interventions weakened several explanations only under their tested transferred recipes. It is unknown whether transfer history differs from fresh runs for reasons beyond seed-dependent optimization, whether a conservative update can preserve the retained policy while changing its residual cases, and whether development-panel measurements predict the official final assessment. No open question is a prescribed next action.
